resolutions.researcher_notes: current_ref (fgw.gxzf.gov.cn) is geo-blocked (ConnectTimeout, no wayback snapshot). Status='operating' is inferable from continuous 2022-2025 activity tied to the Luchuan branch/station rather than a literal status word: gigeps.com 60480.htm (2025-06-16) is a live forestland-restoration/reclamation procurement notice for the Luchuan section right-of-way (standard post-construction, operating-line step); gigeps.com 42701.htm (2024-05-29) is an occupational-health-hazard control evaluation procurement for the staffed, regulated Luchuan facility (service period 2024); cpem.org.cn (Aug 2025 network-milestone article, 广西能源集团/广投管网公司) lists 陆川 (Luchuan) among ten built pipelines in the operator's ~300km network and states the company currently supplies gas daily to 36 downstream users across 13 cities/15 counties in Guangxi. No dormancy signal in any source. Two independent domains (gigeps.com, cpem.org.cn) corroborate ongoing operation.

current_ref (fgw.gxzf.gov.cn) is geo-blocked, no wayback snapshot. Two independent government sources both explicitly name/describe the project as '陆川天然气支线管道工程' (Luchuan NATURAL GAS branch pipeline project): Yulin Emergency Management Bureau safety-condition review letter (yulin.gov.cn, 2019-11-27, addressed to operator 广西广投天然气管网有限公司) and Luchuan County government's own republication of a Yulin Daily article announcing the project's formal approval (luchuan.gov.cn, 2019-05-21). Both confirm Fuel=Gas.

current_ref (news.bjx.com.cn) is a 200-OK Aliyun WAF anti-bot challenge page with zero real article content -- confirmed by direct curl AND by fetching a fresh on-demand wayback capture of the same URL (both return only obfuscated JS challenge code, no Chinese text), so it does not genuinely support ProposalYear=2021/ProposalMonth=3. Fresh search does not support 2021 either: two independent reachable government sources place formal milestones in 2019 -- luchuan.gov.cn (2019-05-21, reporting the autonomous-region DRC's formal project approval/批复) and yulin.gov.cn (2019-11-26/27, safety-condition review passed) -- and a project cannot be formally approved by the government two years before it is first proposed, so ProposalYear=2021 is very likely wrong (consistent with the prior deep-sweep audit's same finding). Not proposing a ref that would misrepresent support for 2021; the true proposal date is probably <=2019 and needs the primary fgw.gxzf.gov.cn approval document (geo-blocked here, no wayback snapshot) to pin down precisely.

current_ref (fgw.gxzf.gov.cn, article title '陆川支线成功投产') is geo-blocked with no wayback snapshot; search-engine indexing of that same dead page is the only place a 2024-06-15 gas-on date appears, so it cannot be cited as a working, independently-fetchable URL. Fresh search for the commissioning event on other reachable hosts (gx.chinanews.com.cn, gx.xinhuanet.com, sogou-indexed news portals, gas.in-en.com [403 on fetch]) did not surface an independently fetchable article stating the exact June 2024 date. Circumstantial-only support found: gigeps.com 42701.htm (occupational-health evaluation procurement for the Luchuan facility, response window closing 2024-06-04) and the cpem.org.cn network article are consistent with a mid-2024 commissioning but do not themselves state a start date, so not cited as refs for this specific value. StartYear1=2024/StartMonth1=6 remains plausible but unresolved pending access to the primary source.

current_ref (fgw.gxzf.gov.cn) is geo-blocked, no wayback snapshot. Two independent, reachable, verified sources were found -- luchuan.gov.cn (2019-05-21: '设计输量为0.84亿立方米/年') and dy.163.com (2020-09-26: '设计年输量为0.85亿m[3]') -- but both report a design ANNUAL throughput (~84-85 million m3/year), which converts to roughly 0.23 million Sm3/day on a straight /365 basis, about 15% above GEM's recorded DAILY Capacity=0.20 mill.Sm3/day. The only source found stating a matching daily figure ('满负荷状态下每天可输送天然气超20万立方米', i.e. >0.20 million Sm3/day at full load) is the dead fgw.gxzf.gov.cn page, search-engine-indexed only, not independently fetchable. Since the two working sources report a different metric (annual, not peak-daily) that does not cleanly match the recorded value, not proposing them as support; flagging the annual-vs-daily distinction for a researcher who can pull the primary document's exact daily-capacity line.

current_ref (fgw.gxzf.gov.cn) is geo-blocked, no wayback snapshot. Two independent, reachable, verified sources both give the pipeline's full length as ~27km: luchuan.gov.cn (2019-05-21, '管道全长约27km') and dy.163.com (2020-09-26, '全长27km，其中福绵境内18km，陆川境内9km'). GEM records LengthKnown=28.00km -- a ~3.6% difference from the two corroborating sources, within the same design-vs-as-built rounding tolerance the prior deep-sweep audit found acceptable for this identical 27-vs-28 gap ('consistent within rounding, not a red flag'). Tier set to medium (not high) to reflect the minor numeric gap even though the two sources independently agree with each other.

current_ref (fgw.gxzf.gov.cn) is geo-blocked, no wayback snapshot. EndLocation='Luchuan' (Yulin/Guangxi) is corroborated by two independent sources: both luchuan.gov.cn and dy.163.com state the line terminates at the Luchuan Distribution Station in Wenquan Town, Luchuan County. However StartLocation='Bobai' is contradicted by the same two sources: both state the pipeline physically starts at the Shatian distribution/pigging station (沙田分输清管站/沙田阀室) in FUMIAN DISTRICT (福绵区), Yulin -- not in Bobai county -- and dy.163.com explicitly attributes the 'Bobai' naming to that station being the terminus of the separately-built Bobai branch pipeline (a naming/attribution nuance, not the literal physical start point). This matches the prior deep-sweep audit's caveat exactly ('tighten StartLocation to the actual physical start (Shatian Town, Fumian District) rather than Bobai'). Since the bundled Location value (Start+End) is only half-supported, not proposing these as refs for the recorded value as-is; flagging for a researcher decision on correcting StartLocation to Shatian/Fumian District.
